page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-16 is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, the configuration maps across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance provision contains neither discrete GPUs nor bundled local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core compute performance alongside predictable multithreaded scalability. The instance attained 2,864.18 in stress-ng single-core tests and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,871.0. Multithreaded execution achieved 22,953.66 in stress-ng and 10,098.0 in Geekbench. Cryptographic and compression tests demonstrate steady throughput, registering 27.81 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 55.54 GB/sec in multithreaded bzip3 decompression. However, memory subsystem tests exhibit performance variation: while small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 1,132.17 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB block writes decline to 13.03 GB/sec, indicating potential bandwidth contention for large unbuffered transfers.

With its standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides dependable resource allocation for common enterprise footprints. In application workloads, it sustains 20.9 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and delivers 14.22 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Light machine learning inference performs well with smaller models, reaching 285.78 tokens per second on 135M parameter generation, whereas large 70B models encounter severe execution constraints. The c3d-standard-16 is aligned with backend web serving, enterprise application servers, caching infrastructure, and build systems.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9B14 processor using x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores, paired with 64 GB of RAM to maintain a standard 1:4 resource allocation ratio. The hardware supports extended instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, BF16, and hardware-accelerated cryptography. No local storage or discrete GPUs are bundled, necessitating external block storage solutions. Performance testing reveals strong single-core compute results, balanced multithreaded output, and 20.9 million operations per second on Redis benchmarks. While small cached memory operations perform at high rates, large uncached memory write throughput exhibits latency bottlenecks. With reliable dedicated core execution, this instance is suited for enterprise web serving, microservices architectures, caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines requiring consistent processor availability.
